titulo: Looking Forward – Predicting and Planning for the Future
titulo_es: Mirar adelante: predecir y planear el futuro
estandares: Proyecto planes y predicciones con distintos matices temporales. Comprendo y produzco textos sobre salud y bienestar, y doy consejos fundamentados.
competencias: Usar futuro simple, continuo, perfecto y perfecto continuo; construir condicionales de tipo cero y uno; manejar fechas y ordinales; describir el cuerpo, la salud y hábitos saludables.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante diseña un plan personal de bienestar a cinco años: qué estará haciendo, qué habrá logrado para cada fecha y qué pasará si mantiene o abandona cada hábito.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student designs a personal five-year wellbeing plan: what they will be doing, what they will have achieved by each date and what will happen if they keep or drop each habit.

lecciones.t: Futuro simple: will y going to
lecciones.t_en: Simple future: will and going to
lecciones.content_es:
El reparto de funciones

  • will: predicción por opinión, decisión del momento, promesa, ofrecimiento.
  • going to: intención ya decidida, predicción con evidencia presente.

Matices de certeza

I'm sure it will work. · It will probably take longer. · It might not be enough. · It definitely won't happen this year.

Otras formas para el futuro

  • Presente continuo → cita ya acordada: I'm seeing the doctor at 4.
  • Presente simple → horario: The clinic opens at 7.
  • be about to → inminente: The results are about to come out.

Recordatorio

Después de when, as soon as, before, after, until no se usa will: I'll call you when I get the results.
lecciones.content_en:
Division of roles

  • will: prediction from opinion, on-the-spot decision, promise, offer.
  • going to: an intention already decided, a prediction with present evidence.

Degrees of certainty

I'm sure it will work. · It will probably take longer. · It might not be enough. · It definitely won't happen this year.

Other future forms

  • Present continuous → arranged appointment: I'm seeing the doctor at 4.
  • Present simple → timetable: The clinic opens at 7.
  • be about to → imminent: The results are about to come out.

Reminder

After when, as soon as, before, after, until we do not use will: I'll call you when I get the results.

lecciones.content_es:
Forma

will be + verbo-ing: This time next year I will be studying at university.

Usos

  • Acción en curso en un momento futuro concreto: At 10 tomorrow we'll be taking the exam.
  • Planes que ya siguen su curso natural: I'll be seeing her on Monday anyway.
  • Preguntas educadas y no invasivas: Will you be using the car tonight? (más suave que Will you use…?)

Expresiones que lo acompañan

this time tomorrow, at 8 p.m., all day, during the summer, while you're away.

Diferencia clave

I'll do it at 5 = empezaré a las 5. I'll be doing it at 5 = a las 5 ya estaré en medio de la tarea.
lecciones.content_en:
Form

will be + verb-ing: This time next year I will be studying at university.

Uses

  • An action in progress at a specific future moment: At 10 tomorrow we'll be taking the exam.
  • Plans already running their natural course: I'll be seeing her on Monday anyway.
  • Polite, non-intrusive questions: Will you be using the car tonight? (softer than Will you use…?)

Expressions that go with it

this time tomorrow, at 8 p.m., all day, during the summer, while you're away.

Key difference

I'll do it at 5 = I will start at 5. I'll be doing it at 5 = at 5 I will already be in the middle of it.

lecciones.t: Futuro perfecto y futuro perfecto continuo
lecciones.t_en: Future perfect and future perfect continuous
lecciones.content_es:
Futuro perfecto

will have + participio: acción terminada antes de un momento futuro.
By 2030, I will have finished my degree.

Futuro perfecto continuo

will have been + verbo-ing: enfatiza la duración acumulada hasta ese momento.
By December, I will have been training for two years.

La clave: la expresión de tiempo

  • by + fecha o momento: by next year, by the time you arrive
  • in + periodo: in five years' time

Comparación rápida

  • I will finish → lo terminaré.
  • I will be finishing → estaré terminándolo.
  • I will have finished → ya lo habré terminado.
  • I will have been finishing → llevaré tiempo terminándolo.

Después de by the time el verbo va en presente: By the time you arrive, I'll have left.
lecciones.content_en:
Future perfect

will have + participle: an action finished before a future moment.
By 2030, I will have finished my degree.

Future perfect continuous

will have been + verb-ing: it emphasizes the duration accumulated up to that moment.
By December, I will have been training for two years.

The key: the time expression

  • by + date or moment: by next year, by the time you arrive
  • in + period: in five years' time

Quick comparison

  • I will finish → I will finish it.
  • I will be finishing → I will be in the middle of finishing.
  • I will have finished → I will already have finished.
  • I will have been finishing → I will have spent time finishing.

After by the time the verb goes in the present: By the time you arrive, I'll have left.

lecciones.content_es:
Condicional cero

If + presente, presente: verdades generales y relaciones causa-efecto constantes.
If you don't sleep enough, your immune system weakens.

Con este tipo, if y when son intercambiables.

Primer condicional

If + presente, will + base: consecuencia probable en el futuro.
If you exercise regularly, you will feel better.

Variantes del resultado

  • Modal: If you eat well, you can improve your energy.
  • Imperativo: If you feel dizzy, sit down.
  • Sugerencia: If it hurts, you should see a doctor.

Conectores condicionales

unless (a menos que) · as long as / provided that (siempre que) · in case (por si acaso) · even if (incluso si).

Regla firme: después de todos ellos no va will.
lecciones.content_en:
Zero conditional

If + present, present: general truths and constant cause-effect relations.
If you don't sleep enough, your immune system weakens.

With this type, if and when are interchangeable.

First conditional

If + present, will + base: a likely future consequence.
If you exercise regularly, you will feel better.

Result variants

  • Modal: If you eat well, you can improve your energy.
  • Imperative: If you feel dizzy, sit down.
  • Suggestion: If it hurts, you should see a doctor.

Conditional connectors

unless · as long as / provided that · in case · even if.

Firm rule: after all of them there is no will.

lecciones.content_es:
Ordinales

1st first · 2nd second · 3rd third · 4th fourth · 5th fifth · 8th eighth · 9th ninth · 12th twelfth · 20th twentieth · 21st twenty-first · 30th thirtieth.

Regla: se agrega -th, salvo los tres primeros de cada decena, que usan st, nd y rd.

Fechas completas

Monday, September 21st, 2026 → Monday, September the twenty-first, twenty twenty-six.

Otros usos del ordinal

the first time, the second floor, the third chapter, my twentieth birthday, the 21st century.

Preposiciones

on + día y fecha · in + mes, año, década, siglo · at + hora, festividades.

Duraciones

for two weeks · from Monday to Friday · until June · within a month · in three days' time.
lecciones.content_en:
Ordinals

1st first · 2nd second · 3rd third · 4th fourth · 5th fifth · 8th eighth · 9th ninth · 12th twelfth · 20th twentieth · 21st twenty-first · 30th thirtieth.

Rule: add -th, except the first three of each ten, which take st, nd and rd.

Full dates

Monday, September 21st, 2026 → Monday, September the twenty-first, twenty twenty-six.

Other uses of ordinals

the first time, the second floor, the third chapter, my twentieth birthday, the 21st century.

Prepositions

on + day and date · in + month, year, decade, century · at + clock time, holidays.

Durations

for two weeks · from Monday to Friday · until June · within a month · in three days' time.

lecciones.content_es:
Molestias comunes

a headache, a stomachache, a sore throat, a cough, a fever, a cold, the flu, an allergy, a rash (sarpullido), a sprain (esguince), a broken bone.

Cómo se expresan

  • have + enfermedad: I have a headache.
  • My … hurts: My back hurts.
  • feel + adjetivo: I feel dizzy / sick / weak / exhausted.

En la consulta

What's the matter? · How long have you had it? · Where does it hurt? · Take this twice a day. · Get plenty of rest.

Ojo

the flu lleva artículo; a cold lleva a. Y I feel sick significa tener náuseas o estar enfermo, según el contexto.
lecciones.content_en:
Common complaints

a headache, a stomachache, a sore throat, a cough, a fever, a cold, the flu, an allergy, a rash, a sprain, a broken bone.

How they are expressed

  • have + illness: I have a headache.
  • My … hurts: My back hurts.
  • feel + adjective: I feel dizzy / sick / weak / exhausted.

At the doctor's

What's the matter? · How long have you had it? · Where does it hurt? · Take this twice a day. · Get plenty of rest.

Careful

the flu takes the article; a cold takes a. And I feel sick can mean nauseous or unwell depending on the context.

lecciones.content_es:
Fórmulas de consejo

  • should / shouldn't + base: You should drink more water.
  • ought to: más formal, mismo sentido.
  • had better (+ base): advertencia con consecuencia: You'd better rest, or you'll get worse.
  • Why don't you…? / How about + -ing?: sugerencia amable.
  • If I were you, I would…: consejo empático.
  • It's a good idea to… / Try to…

Hábitos saludables

get enough sleep, stay hydrated, eat a balanced diet, exercise regularly, take breaks, limit screen time, manage stress, ask for help.

Ojo

had better es más fuerte que should: implica que algo malo puede pasar si no se hace. Y How about va con gerundio: How about going for a walk?
lecciones.content_en:
Advice formulas

  • should / shouldn't + base: You should drink more water.
  • ought to: more formal, same meaning.
  • had better (+ base): a warning with a consequence: You'd better rest, or you'll get worse.
  • Why don't you…? / How about + -ing?: a friendly suggestion.
  • If I were you, I would…: empathetic advice.
  • It's a good idea to… / Try to…

Healthy habits

get enough sleep, stay hydrated, eat a balanced diet, exercise regularly, take breaks, limit screen time, manage stress, ask for help.

Careful

had better is stronger than should: it implies something bad may happen otherwise. And How about takes a gerund: How about going for a walk?

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

El futuro en inglés tiene cuatro capas: simple (will / going to), continuo (en curso), perfecto (terminado antes de una fecha) y perfecto continuo (duración acumulada). Los condicionales cero y uno enlazan condición y consecuencia.

Puntos gramaticales

  • will be + -ing para lo que estará en curso.
  • will have + participio para lo que ya estará terminado.
  • Después de if, when, unless, as long as y by the time no va will.
  • had better + base es una advertencia; How about + gerundio es una sugerencia.

Vocabulario

Ordinales y fechas, partes del cuerpo y bienestar, enfermedades con have y hurt, y fórmulas de consejo.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The English future has four layers: simple (will / going to), continuous (in progress), perfect (finished before a date) and perfect continuous (accumulated duration). Zero and first conditionals link condition and consequence.

Grammar points

  • will be + -ing for what will be in progress.
  • will have + participle for what will already be finished.
  • After if, when, unless, as long as and by the time there is no will.
  • had better + base is a warning; How about + gerund is a suggestion.

Vocabulary

Ordinals and dates, body parts and wellbeing, illnesses with have and hurt, and advice formulas.
puntos_clave: will be + -ing = en curso en un momento futuro.
will be + -ing = in progress at a future moment.
will have + participio = terminado antes de esa fecha.
will have + participle = finished before that date.
Por the time y as soon as van con presente, no con will.
by the time and as soon as take the present, not will.
unless ya es negativo: no se le agrega not.
unless is already negative: do not add not.
the flu lleva the; a cold lleva a.
flu takes the; a cold takes a.
had better + verbo base, sin to.
had better + base verb, with no to.
